newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER-MANCHESTER UNITED'S TEAM BUS ATTACKED IN ISTANBUL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MANCHESTER UNITED'S TEAM BUS ATTACKED IN ISTANBUL.

text.p: Turkish fans attacked the Manchester United team bus on its way to Istanbul airport after the English team beat Fenerbahce 2-0 in a European Champions' League match on Wednesday night.
Four of United's young players had a narrow escape when a stone smashed through a side window of the bus which was under police escort.
It showered brothers Phil and Gary Neville, Paul Scholes and Ben Thornley with glass but none of them were hurt.

Phil Neville said: "It was a real shock but fortunately none of us were hurt. We all got showered by glass and I got some of it in my mouth but it did not do any damage -- I was able to just spit it out.
"We were all a bit shaken but the coach did not stop and it was not as bad as it could have been."
The incident happened as the coach approached the giant suspension bridge across the Bosphorous.
It was the culmination to a night of intimidation for the English champions, whose small band of 300 fans suffered a hale of missiles after Eric Cantona scored the decisive second goal.
That disturbance was quelled by riot police who had managed to protect the United team until the stone-throwing incident.
